title: bench: add bursty-mix fragmentation scenario + baseline artifacts
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Context
We’ve been missing a repeatable benchmark that reproduces the production failure mode we’ve seen during bursty arrivals + mixed context lengths: KV cache fragmentation leading to allocator churn and p95/p99 spikes (and occasional OOM / admission-control clampdown). This PR adds a new scenario to benchmark-lab that (a) measures fragmentation ratio and allocator pressure over time and (b) makes tail latency deltas visible when runtime changes (eviction/compaction) land.

What’s in this PR
- New scenario: bursty_mixed_lengths_multi_tenant_v1
  - Bursty arrival model (configurable on/off bursts) with prefill/decode interleaving.
  - Sequence-length distribution mixture (short chat, medium, long-context) with skew knobs.
  - Multi-tenant pool simulation via request classes (tier + concurrency caps) to mimic shared hosted pools.
- New metrics emitted to the benchmark artifact bundle:
  - kv_fragmentation_ratio (defined as 1 - (used_pages / allocated_pages) at the allocator layer; see notes below)
  - kv_alloc_failures_total (per run, plus time series)
  - kv_evictions_total / kv_eviction_bytes_total
  - compaction_events_total + compaction_bytes_moved_total (present but optional; scenario should work pre-compaction)
  - latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) per phase (prefill vs decode) + overall
- Baseline results & artifacts published under the standard artifact layout:
  - results/baselines/2025-02/bursty-mix-v1/*.csv
  - results/baselines/2025-02/bursty-mix-v1/README.md (methodology + interpretation)
  - Grafana-ready JSON timeseries (artifact only; no dashboard changes here)
- Regression gate hooks:
  - Adds the scenario to the default nightly suite (but marked non-blocking until perf-canary wiring lands).
  - Adds a local "--smoke" mode to keep developer iteration under ~8 minutes.

Metric definitions / notes
- kv_fragmentation_ratio in this harness is intentionally allocator-centric (page/block utilization), not raw CUDA allocator fragmentation. The goal is to detect pathological holes that increase search/relocation and drive tail spikes.
- For runs where the runtime does not export these counters yet, the harness will record "N/A" for the KV metrics and still report latency. (This is important so we can land the scenario before the full runtime metrics rollout.)

Baseline summary (from artifact README)
- Worst-case tail behavior appears when long-context share exceeds ~20% and burst factor >= 3x.
- In the baseline region/pool config, p99 decode latency spikes correlate with periods where kv_fragmentation_ratio > 0.35 and kv_evictions_total increases sharply.
- One model family shows a different signature: fewer alloc failures but higher eviction bytes (likely larger KV footprint per token); included in baselines as separate table.

Why this is safe
- Scenario is additive; no existing scenarios are modified aside from shared harness refactors.
- Nightly suite inclusion is non-blocking and can be toggled off via BENCHMARK_LAB_ENABLE_BURSTY_MIX=0.

Follow-ups
- Wire scenario into perf-canary gating once runtime compaction flag is available in canary images (tracked in ENG-2854).
- Revisit fragmentation ratio formula once allocator block semantics (movable vs pinned) are finalized (ADR-0127).

Screenshots / artifacts
- See CI artifact: "bursty_mixed_lengths_multi_tenant_v1-baseline" (contains CSV tables + timeseries JSON + flamegraphs for the harness overhead).

Refs
- Linear: ENG-2843 (Perf suite: add bursty-mix benchmark scenario)
- Related runtime work: ENG-2841 (KV cache compaction improvements)
- Support signal: SUP-4410 (Hosted API timeouts during high load)

Checklist
- [x] Scenario deterministic with fixed seeds
- [x] Smoke mode documented
- [x] Baseline artifacts checked in
- [x] CI runtime pinned to avoid drift
- [x] Added "known limitations" section to artifact README

review_conversation:
Marcus Reed (review): Baseline tables look useful. Two requests: (1) ensure we separate prefill vs decode percentiles in the CSV because decode tail is what we care about; (2) define fragmentation ratio precisely in docs/metrics.md.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Done. Added per-phase latency columns to baseline_summary.csv and expanded docs/metrics.md with the allocator-centric definition + caveats.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Can we make sure this scenario still runs on older runtime images where the KV metrics aren’t present yet? I don’t want this blocked on the runtime PR.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Yep—kv_cache.py now treats missing counters as optional and emits N/A. Added a unit test that feeds a log without kv_fragmentation_ratio and asserts artifact generation still succeeds.

Allison Grant (review): Please align metric names with what SRE expects (suffixes, units). Also, the timeseries JSON should include region/pool/model labels if present.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated metric keys to match the proposed naming (kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_alloc_failures_total, etc.) and added label passthrough when the log provides them. Included an example labeled timeseries in the artifact README.

Yuki Sato (review): Minor: the burst schedule default seems too aggressive for dev laptops; smoke mode should reduce concurrency and tokens.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Adjusted --smoke defaults (lower concurrency, smaller max_new_tokens, shorter duration). Verified smoke completes in ~6–7 minutes on my machine.

Marcus Reed (review): Approved. Let’s land as non-blocking nightly first and then promote once perf-canary is wired.

Merge: Squash merge approved and completed.
release_notes: Added benchmark scenario `bursty_mixed_lengths_multi_tenant_v1` to measure KV cache fragmentation ratio and burst-driven tail latency; published Feb 2025 baseline artifacts and integrated scenario into nightly suite (non-blocking).
